page: Microsoft Azure D16ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dadsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with 16 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz and includes 48 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core, and includes a 945 GB local NVMe SSD.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core score, and single-threaded gzip compression all placing in the top tier (top 10%). Text processing also ranks in the top tier. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores, falls within the average range (middle 50%). Memory bandwidth tests, such as read-only large block at 50.99 GB/sec and write large block at 34.16 GB/sec, also align with average tier performance.

For machine learning workloads, the server demonstrates strong prompt processing and top-tier text generation speeds when running small (135M) LLM models. However, performance scales down on larger models, with medium (7B) model inference processing at average speeds, and large (70B) model prompt processing falling into the weak category (bottom 25%). The instance supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration (AES, VAES, SHA_NI), but lacks AMX support.

Given its balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio and integrated local NVMe storage, this instance offers a resource-dense profile for general-purpose workloads. It is suited for applications requiring high single-thread performance, software compilation, database operations, and web serving. The inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage supports workloads requiring fast temporary storage without the overhead of external disks.
